gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Techaeris (Alex Hernandez, 2026-10-02) used the TESSAN TC03 at IFA 2026 to run camera battery chargers, laptop bricks and electric trimmers through its 110 V outlets, reporting no buzzing, whining or excessive heat. That is the only hands-on use by a named reviewer found for any candidate, and it includes no instrument readings.
standout_why: ChatGPT's results that carry product detail are maker manuals for TESSAN TS-TC02, TUS-2 and the unnamed TESSAN 220V to 110V converter, Foval and EPICKA, plus the Digital Camera World Ceptics review. The manuals give specs only, and no reviewer tested anything in them. The Digital Camera World page would not load (WebFetch returned only the title, the ?amp variant gave the same, archive.org is blocked and the inkl copy returned 403), so I can't rule out that it holds Ceptics test detail. That uncertainty is why this scores 1 rather than 2. I also tried travelpowerpro.com, which failed on a TLS certificate error. I did not open voltwander, momax, globalplugs, doace, culturecolumn or cabinandcarry. None of the angle's real target exists among the rivals or anywhere else I looked: no named reviewer or lab published an output-voltage, waveform, temperature, efficiency or USB-PD measurement for TESSAN TC03, BESTEK 250W, Foval or Ceptics. Techaeris, Gadget Flow and This Old House all print spec figures only.
decides: It confirms the TESSAN TC03 as the pick for low-wattage US electronics and trimmers: a named reviewer used it on a work trip and reported no noise or heat. It doesn't separate the TC03 from BESTEK or Foval, because no reviewer measured any of them. It also supports the 250 W limit. Techaeris lists hair dryers, curling irons, flat irons, steamers, kettles and travel irons as loads that trip the overload protection, so the page should send heat-tool users elsewhere.

findings.label: Named hands-on use (no instrument readings)
findings.value: Ran camera battery chargers, laptop bricks and electric trimmers at IFA 2026 'without buzzing, whining, or emitting excessive heat'

findings.note: Alex Hernandez, Techaeris, 2026-10-02. Qualitative. The review gives no measured voltage, temperature, dB or charging watts, and no wattages for the devices tested. Hernandez found it 'almost the only adapter I needed at IFA 2026'.

findings.label: Loads the reviewer says trip it
findings.value: Hair dryers, curling irons, garment steamers, flat irons, electric kettles, travel irons (over the 250 W combined ceiling)
findings.source_title: TESSAN TC03 Voltage Converter Review | Techaeris
findings.note: Alex Hernandez, 2026-10-02. The 250 W limit is the maker's rating, not a load test. He also notes the unit can feel top-heavy with two AC cords and pull out of loose European sockets, and that all four USB ports share one bus, so charging slows when several devices draw at once.

findings.label: Weight as published by reviewers (spec, not weighed)

findings.source_title: TESSAN 250W voltage converter travel adapter (TC03) review | Gadget Flow
findings.note: Gadget Flow review by Madhurima Nag, 2026-08-20, with no testing; all figures are TESSAN specs (220–230 V in, 110 V out, 250 W, USB-C up to 20 W, $43.99).
